title: Examplozumab and heart failure hospitalisation: a randomised, placebo-controlled trial
abstract: BACKGROUND: Examplozumab is an investigational antibody for chronic heart failure. METHODS: We randomly assigned 1,204 adults with chronic heart failure to examplozumab or placebo and followed them for a median of 24 months. RESULTS: Hospitalisation for heart failure occurred in 18.2% of the examplozumab group and 23.9% of the placebo group (hazard ratio [HR] 0.74; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.61 to 0.90; P=0.002). All-cause mortality did not differ significantly between groups (HR 0.93; 95% CI 0.76 to 1.14; P=0.48). CONCLUSIONS: Examplozumab reduced heart failure hospitalisation but not mortality.

title: Examplozumab use and 30-day readmission in a national heart failure registry
abstract: Aims: To assess real-world readmission after examplozumab. Methods and results: In a registry cohort of 3,416 patients (mean age 71 years), examplozumab use was associated with lower odds of 30-day readmission (adjusted odds ratio 0.81, 95% CI 0.70-0.94, p=0.006). A risk model predicting readmission achieved an AUC of 0.77 (95% CI 0.74-0.80) in the validation set. Conclusion: Findings are consistent with trial results.

title: Effect of examplozumab on exercise capacity: a pilot trial
abstract: Sixty-two participants with stable heart failure were randomised to examplozumab or usual care for 12 weeks. The change in 6-minute walk distance favoured examplozumab (mean difference 18.5 m, 90% CI 4.2 to 32.8). Quality-of-life scores did not change. Larger trials are needed.

title: Long-term outcomes with examplozumab: extended follow-up of a multicentre cohort
abstract: Background We followed 2 870 patients for up to 5 years. Findings Cardiovascular death occurred in 312 patients. Examplozumab was not associated with cardiovascular death (hazard ratio 1·02, 95% CI 0·88–1·18; p=0·79). Interpretation Benefits on hospitalisation did not translate into lower cardiovascular mortality.

title: An NT-proBNP threshold to select patients for examplozumab
abstract: Objective: To evaluate an NT-proBNP threshold of 900 pg/mL for selecting treatment candidates. Methods: We studied 512 patients referred to two clinics. Results: The threshold had a sensitivity of 88% (95% CI 83 to 92) and a specificity of 71% (95% CI 66 to 76) against the expert panel decision. Conclusion: The threshold may support triage.

title: Dust attenuation and star formation in high-redshift galaxies
abstract: We measured dust attenuation in 184 galaxies at redshift 2 to 3 using deep infrared imaging. Attenuation was correlated with stellar mass (r = 0.62, 95% CI 0.48 to 0.73). Star-forming galaxies above 10^10 solar masses showed systematically higher attenuation. These results constrain models of early galaxy evolution.

title: Examplozumab: promise and open questions (editorial)
abstract: Examplozumab has attracted attention after several studies in heart failure. In this editorial we discuss the design of the published trials, the limits of registry data and the questions a larger outcome trial should answer, including effects on mortality and quality of life.
